# Kickoff research (2026-11-04)

Three research passes at kickoff (market, runtime, integrations). Facts as of
2026-11-04; re-check any fact before relying on it weeks later. Full source
lists were in the research reports; the key links are kept here.

## Market

- The dictated names: xAI **Grok Bot** (beta 11 Aug 2026, https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot),
  OpenAI **dots** (DevDay 29 Sep 2026), Anthropic **Claude Duet** (research preview 21 Oct 2026,
  https://claude.com/product/claude-duet). Also Google Gemini Spark (May 2026), Meta Muse (Sep 2026).
  ChatGPT Pulse retired Jun 2026 (replaced by scheduled tasks).
- **Common now** (judges have seen it): morning brief from mail and calendar; "what did I miss";
  meeting note-taker bots; always-on agents with approval cards.
- **Still rare** (the pitch): set up by the company from org data; code-aware (upstream change x
  owned service x uncommitted work); a labelled away-mode stand-in in Slack with sources, a
  reviewable log and per-recipient sharing; a labelled AI speaking in a live meeting (rarest, and
  where the bans and lawsuits are).
- Closest: Viven (colleagues query your "twin", reactive only); Grok Bot shared bots (its Slack
  posts as you); dots (answers only you by default); Zoom AI Companion (joins "on your behalf",
  notes only); Otter Meeting Agent (speaks when asked); Glean (editable profile of role and goals).
- Backlash: Otter class action survived dismissal (Aug 2026); Teams holds outside bots in the lobby
  and lets admins block them (Aug 2026); Amazon blocked Meta Muse for not identifying as an agent
  (Sep 2026); 341 malicious ClawHub skills (Feb 2026); Gartner "Block Personal AI Assistants"
  (Feb 2026); dots went off-task in 8.6% (5 chained tasks) to 19.7% (10) of OpenAI's tests.
- Slack API terms restrict bulk export, permanent copies and large-language-model use of Slack data by apps; Slack
  offers live real-time search (GA Feb 2026). Rule for us: store facts plus links, not copies.
- **Copy**: quiet by default with a daily ping cap; draft, then approve (allow once / always here /
  deny; stale asks expire); its own labelled identity that announces itself; content is data,
  never instructions; an editable "what I know about you" page and a "who asked what" log.
- **Avoid**: silent meeting recording; posting as the employee; broad access plus third-party
  skills plus bulk copies of Slack.

## Runtime (checked on the build machine: Claude Code 2.1.318, codex-cli 0.153.4)

- **Best**: our own always-on program (daemon) collects events without AI and starts a short,
  fresh headless run per batch of new items. Rejected for the core: `/loop` (recurring tasks
  expire after 7 days, fire only while the session is open, compaction drifts); channels (only
  allowlisted plugins; custom channels only in interactive sessions); cloud routines (preview,
  at most hourly, heavy per run). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks
- Claude headless: `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema <schema> --permission-mode dontAsk
  --allowedTools <list> --mcp-config <file> --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence`.
  Since v2.1.302 a `-p` run starts in Manual mode unless a mode is set. Skills load in `-p`
  (not with `--bare`). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless
- **Trap**: the docs say `--bare` will become the `-p` default, and bare mode never reads OAuth, so
  a subscription `-p` would stop authenticating. **Pin the CLI version.**
- Codex headless: `codex exec --json --output-schema <file> --sandbox read-only --ephemeral
  --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir>`. Skills in `.agents/skills` (whether they load in `exec`:
  unverified). MCP in `config.toml`.
- **Policy**: our own script driving the unmodified Claude Code CLI on the owner's own Max login is
  permitted; third-party tools using subscription OAuth are not
  (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance). `codex exec` on a ChatGPT login is a
  documented "advanced" path; OpenAI recommends an API key for automation. Max includes $100 a
  month of API credits since 7 Oct 2026 (Agent SDK, or `-p` with an API key).
- At the company: sending company Slack or mail through a personal consumer plan is a company
  policy question; at Airbnb use the company harness and its auth.
- Limits: Max runs per hour are not published; log the usage each run's JSON returns.
- Portability: skills live in `.claude/skills` (Claude) vs `.agents/skills` (Codex): keep one real
  folder and link the other (whether Claude follows the link: unverified). MCP config is JSON
  (`.mcp.json`) vs TOML (`config.toml`): generate both from one source. Never hard-code MCP tool
  names in skill text.
- **Pattern: the AI proposes, the program acts.** The run returns proposed actions as JSON; the
  daemon executes, logs and gates them. One `run_agent(prompt, schema)` function with a Claude and
  a Codex backend; switch backend when one hits its limit.
- 24-hour machine later: the same daemon under systemd; `claude setup-token` gives a 1-year token
  (model calls only, no claude.ai connectors).

## Integrations

- **Slack**: one internal app with Socket Mode (no public URL). The bot token posts as the app
  (labelled) and replies in threads; a user token from the same app reads the owner's DMs.
  Internal apps are exempt from the 2025 rate-limit cut. Free plan: 90 days of history visible,
  10 apps (seed demo data inside 90 days). Official Slack MCP (GA Feb 2026): user tokens only,
  acts as the user, no events. Open source: korotovsky/slack-mcp-server.
- **Google (personal)**: one Cloud project, External consent with a test user, a Desktop OAuth
  client. **Refresh tokens expire after 7 days while the app is in Testing**: keep a one-command
  re-login. taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp (MIT). Official Google MCP servers: developer
  preview, Workspace accounts, Gmail drafts only. Poll (Gmail `history.list`, Calendar
  `syncToken`); export Docs as markdown through Drive.
- **GitHub**: official MCP server (has a read-only mode). ETag-poll the upstream repo's commits and
  releases (a 304 costs no rate limit); the compare API gives changed files to match against our
  imports and lockfiles.
- **Meetings (hardest)**: since 2 Mar 2026 a Zoom Meeting SDK bot joining a meeting hosted by
  another Zoom account needs an "on behalf of" token: the authorizing user must be in the meeting
  (https://developers.zoom.us/docs/meeting-sdk/obf-faq/). So "attend while I'm away" works only
  for meetings in the account that owns the Zoom app. Zoom Basic caps meetings at 40 min.
  Bot services: Recall.ai ($0.50/h, first 5 h free, plays MP3 audio or a web page as camera and
  mic), Attendee (5 h free hosted, speech endpoint), joinly (MCP `speak_text`, local).
  **Google Meet is easier for the demo** (no app, the host admits the bot).
  Minimum: bot joins a meeting we host, transcript, summary. Speaking: the update is drafted and
  approved in advance, rendered to MP3, played on cue, also posted in the meeting chat.
- **Voice**: ElevenLabs (about 100 ms; already used for the film). OpenAI TTS models shut down
  6 Jan 2027.
- **Integration contract** (vendor-neutral): `sense(cursor) -> events, next_cursor`;
  `search(query)`; `get(ref)`; `act(action, target, payload, idempotency_key)`. Event: id, source,
  kind, at, actor, ref, thread_ref, text, url. Plus a person map across systems, a capability list
  per adapter, an approval gate with dry run, and an audit log. **MCP alone cannot push events,
  so a small collector daemon is needed.**
- **Memory**: one markdown file per entity (people, projects, services, repos, decisions, threads)
  with frontmatter (system ids, aliases, sources), an `index.md`, an append-only log, and SQLite
  full-text search (also holds events, cursors and links). Karpathy's "LLM wiki" pattern (Apr 2026),
  the same shape as Claude Code memory and OpenClaw memory. No embeddings or graph database.
- **Top build risks**: (1) a speaking meeting bot, Zoom above all; (2) push-style sensing;
  (3) Google OAuth friction.
